# Next.js rules

Apply these rules to every Next.js file you write or review. TypeScript style is in `typescript-rules` and React in `react-rules`. The first section is always in force; open a rule from the table when the task touches it. Procedures to set up env validation, logging, the ServiceError class or toasts are in `setup-app-infrastructure`.

## Always apply (critical)

### Check the session and the right to the resource inside every server action

_critical · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Start every server action by reading the session on the server and calling `unauthorized()` when there is none, then run the feature's `canX` check from `permissions.ts` and call `forbidden()` when it fails. Do this in the action itself, even when the page already checked. The service runs the same check in its own guard chain, because routes and jobs call it too.

**Why.** Anyone can call an exported action directly with a crafted POST, so an action that relies on the page's guard lets a signed-out user, or another user, change data they do not own.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
export async function deleteBudget(budgetId: string): ActionResponse<null> {
  const [error] = await removeBudget(budgetId); // the page checked the session
  return error ? { success: false, error: "Could not delete" } : { success: true, data: null };
}
```

**Correct:**

```ts
export async function deleteBudget(budgetId: string): ActionResponse<null> {
  const { isAuthenticated, userId } = await auth();
  if (!isAuthenticated) unauthorized();
  const [permissionError] = await canEditBudget(userId, budgetId);
  if (permissionError) forbidden();
  const [error] = await removeBudget({ userId, budgetId });
  return error ? { success: false, error: "Could not delete" } : { success: true, data: null };
}
```

**Exceptions.** Without `experimental.authInterrupts`, redirect to sign-in instead of `unauthorized()` and call `notFound()` instead of `forbidden()`.

### Re-validate every action input with the schema's safeParse and return its fieldErrors

_critical · typescript, nextjs, zod@>=4_

**Rule.** Parse every action argument with the feature's Zod schema using `safeParse`, use only `parsed.data` afterwards, and on failure return `{ success: false, error, fieldErrors: z.flattenError(parsed.error).fieldErrors }`. Do this even when the form already validated with the same schema.

**Why.** A TypeScript parameter type is erased at runtime, so an action that trusts it writes whatever a crafted request sends: a negative amount, another user's id, or a 10 MB string.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
export async function createBudget(input: BudgetInput): ActionResponse<Budget> {
  const [error, budget] = await insertBudget(input); // validated only in the browser
  ...
```

**Correct:**

```ts
export async function createBudget(input: BudgetInput): ActionResponse<Budget> {
  const parsed = budgetSchema.safeParse(input);
  if (!parsed.success) {
    return { success: false, error: "Check the form", fieldErrors: z.flattenError(parsed.error).fieldErrors };
  }
  const [error, budget] = await insertBudget(parsed.data);
  ...
```

**Exceptions.** On Zod 3, use `parsed.error.flatten().fieldErrors`.

### Mark server modules with import "server-only" and never import server/ from client code

_critical · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Start every module in `features/{domain}/server/` that is not a `"use server"` action file (services, db, api, `permissions.ts`) with `import "server-only"`. Never import anything from `server/` in a `"use client"` file or in a module a client file imports; client code takes types from `types/` and actions as props.

**Why.** A server module reached from client code ships its queries, internal rules and whatever it reads to the browser bundle, and without the `server-only` marker the build succeeds, so the leak is found only by someone reading the shipped JavaScript.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
"use client";
import { InvoiceStatus } from "~/features/invoices/server/db/schema";
import { formatTotal } from "~/features/invoices/server/services/invoice.service";
```

**Correct:**

```ts
// features/invoices/server/services/invoice.service.ts
import "server-only";

// features/invoices/components/invoice-row.tsx ("use client")
import { InvoiceStatus, type ClientInvoiceListItem } from "~/features/invoices/types";
```

### Never put a secret in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable or in the client schema

_critical · typescript, nextjs, t3-env_

**Rule.** Declare a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable only in the `client` schema of `data/env/client.ts`, and only for a value meant to be public: a publishable key, a public URL, an analytics id. A secret key, token, private key or connection string goes in the `server` schema without the prefix and is read only in server code.

**Why.** Next.js inlines every `NEXT_PUBLIC_` value into the JavaScript sent to the browser at build time, so a secret given the prefix is published to every visitor and must be rotated.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
// data/env/client.ts
client: {
  NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: z.string().startsWith("sk_"),
},
```

**Correct:**

```ts
// data/env/server.ts
server: { STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: z.string().startsWith("sk_") },

// data/env/client.ts
client: { NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: z.string().startsWith("pk_") },
```

### Return a fixed user-safe message to the client, never the internal error text

_critical · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Put only a message you wrote for the user in an action's `error`, a route handler's JSON body or a toast. Log the caught error on the server with `log.withError(error)` and its ids; never send `error.message`, a stack, an error code from a driver, or record ids and roles in the message.

**Why.** A raw message leaks table names, SQL fragments, internal hostnames or another user's data to whoever submits the form, and the toast cookie is readable by any script on the page.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
if (error) {
  return { success: false, error: error.message }; // 'duplicate key value violates "budgets_name_key"'
}
```

**Correct:**

```ts
if (error) {
  log.withError(error).withMetadata({ userId, operation: "createBudget" }).error("Budget creation failed");
  return { success: false, error: "Could not create the budget" };
}
```

**Exceptions.** A `ServiceError` built by your own code for a validation or business rule (`ServiceError.validation("You can have at most 20 budgets")`) carries a message written for the user and may be returned as is.

### Never log a secret or personal data; log an id, a masked value or a derived flag

_critical · typescript, loglayer_

**Rule.** Never pass a secret (password, token, API key, session id, cookie, `Authorization` header) or personal data (email, phone number, address, date of birth, card or bank number, health data) to a log call, nor a whole object that may contain one, such as a request, its headers or a provider response. Log the identifier (`userId`), a masked form (`maskEmail(email)`) or a derived signal (`hasAuthHeader: true`).

**Why.** A secret written to a log is copied into every log store, backup and aggregator that receives it and must be treated as leaked; personal data there breaks data-protection duties and outlives deletion requests.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
log.withMetadata({ email, password, headers: request.headers }).info("Sign-in attempt");
```

**Correct:**

```ts
log
  .withMetadata({ email: maskEmail(email), hasAuthHeader: request.headers.has("authorization") })
  .info("Sign-in attempt");
```

### Check the session first in the loadData of every protected page

_critical · typescript, nextjs_

**Rule.** Make the session check the first statement of the `loadData` of every protected page, and of any layout `loadData` that reads user data, before any read. Do not count a guard in a parent layout or in `proxy.ts` as the page's guard.

**Why.** A page that relies on its layout's guard serves its data to a signed-out user: layouts do not re-render on client navigation and do not stop child segments from rendering, and a proxy check only reads the cookie optimistically.

**Incorrect:**

```tsx
// app/(app)/layout.tsx guards the group, so the page skips it
async function loadData(invoiceId: string) {
  const [error, invoice] = await getInvoice(invoiceId);
  if (error?.isNotFound) notFound();
  if (error) throw new Error("Failed to load the invoice", { cause: error });
  return { invoice };
}
```

**Correct:**

```tsx
async function loadData(invoiceId: string) {
  const { isAuthenticated, userId } = await auth();
  if (!isAuthenticated) unauthorized();

  const [error, invoice] = await getInvoice(userId, invoiceId);
  if (error?.isNotFound || error?.isPermissionDenied) notFound();
  if (error) throw new Error("Failed to load the invoice", { cause: error });
  return { invoice };
}
```

**Exceptions.** A public page (one `proxy.ts` lets through) has no guard unless the data it reads belongs to a user. Without `experimental.authInterrupts`, call `redirect("/sign-in")` instead of `unauthorized()`.

| medium | [Choose the log level by what the event means; log an expected not-found at warn](references/rules.md#choose-the-log-level-by-what-the-event-means-log-an-expected-not-found-at-warn) — error for a failure to investigate, warn for an expected outcome such as not-found, info for normal events. | typescript, loglayer |
| medium | [Create the request id once in proxy.ts and forward it on the request headers](references/rules.md#create-the-request-id-once-in-proxyts-and-forward-it-on-the-request-headers) — proxy.ts mints requestId and forwards x-request-id on the request and response; handlers read it, never mint one. | typescript, nextjs, loglayer |
| medium | [Log a returned error once, in the action or route handler that decides what to do with it](references/rules.md#log-a-returned-error-once-in-the-action-or-route-handler-that-decides-what-to-do-with-it) — Db and service functions return [error, null] silently; the action or handler logs it once with errorCode and ids. | typescript, loglayer |
| medium | [Log to stdout through Pino everywhere and add the tmp/app.log file only in development](references/rules.md#log-to-stdout-through-pino-everywhere-and-add-the-tmpapplog-file-only-in-development) — PinoTransport writes to stdout everywhere; LogFileRotationTransport is added only when NODE_ENV is development. | typescript, loglayer, pino |
| medium | [Set the logger's level from LOG_LEVEL in the server env, chosen per environment](references/rules.md#set-the-loggers-level-from-log_level-in-the-server-env-chosen-per-environment) — LOG_LEVEL is a validated enum in data/env/server.ts (debug locally, info in production) that lib/logger.ts reads. | typescript, loglayer, pino, t3-env |
| medium | [Name log fields from the shared vocabulary, one name per concept](references/rules.md#name-log-fields-from-the-shared-vocabulary-one-name-per-concept) — userId, requestId, operation, durationMs, errorCode, isRetryable, statusCode, path, method; never uid or user_id. | typescript, loglayer |
| medium | [Await params and searchParams once at the top and pass plain values down](references/rules.md#await-params-and-searchparams-once-at-the-top-and-pass-plain-values-down) — The page or layout awaits the route promises itself; loadData and components receive strings, never a promise. | typescript, nextjs |
| medium | [Compose a page from feature components, with no PageContent wrapper](references/rules.md#compose-a-page-from-feature-components-with-no-pagecontent-wrapper) — Page JSX only arranges components from features/{domain}/components; no business logic, no route-local components. | typescript, nextjs |
| medium | [Keep a layout that reads no data synchronous, with no loadData](references/rules.md#keep-a-layout-that-reads-no-data-synchronous-with-no-loaddata) — A layout only wraps children unless its chrome needs data; auth for its pages is checked in each page, not here. | typescript, nextjs |
| medium | [Let non-critical chrome data fail silently, with the chrome degrading](references/rules.md#let-non-critical-chrome-data-fail-silently-with-the-chrome-degrading) — A badge or counter that fails to load is logged and left out; it never sends the whole route to an error page. | typescript, nextjs |
| medium | [Wire server actions into client components from the page, as props](references/rules.md#wire-server-actions-into-client-components-from-the-page-as-props) — The page or layout imports the action and passes it down; a client component never imports from server/actions. | typescript, nextjs |
| medium | [Render chrome inline in page.tsx when it depends on the page's own data](references/rules.md#render-chrome-inline-in-pagetsx-when-it-depends-on-the-pages-own-data) — Skip layout.tsx for a lone route or chrome built from the page's resource; the page renders header and footer itself. | typescript, nextjs |
| medium | [Type pages and layouts with the generated PageProps and LayoutProps helpers](references/rules.md#type-pages-and-layouts-with-the-generated-pageprops-and-layoutprops-helpers) — Route-generated helpers keep params, searchParams and slots in step with the folders; no hand-written prop types. | typescript, nextjs |
| medium | [Export static metadata unless the title needs data from the route](references/rules.md#export-static-metadata-unless-the-title-needs-data-from-the-route) — List and fixed pages export a metadata object; only detail pages under a [param] segment use generateMetadata. | typescript, nextjs |
